sections.heading: Keep the Washington site visible
sections.text: The archived January 16, 2025 release names Camas as one of three Analog Devices locations. sections.heading: The shared proposal does not create another award
sections.text: Up to US$105 million is the retained proposed ceiling across Camas, Beaverton and Chelmsford. Repeating that number in this account must not create a separate Camas award or a site allocation. Neither equal division nor an inference from another site’s work establishes the Camas amount. The preliminary terms are non-binding and historical; the account does not claim a current final agreement or assume an unchanged present project status from the absence of a later retained record.

sections.heading: Compare milestones only after matching their definitions
sections.text: A useful comparison with Beaverton would identify each facility’s process, product qualification, acceptance basis and observation period. Common mature-node terminology is not evidence of equivalent products, capacity or reliability. A shipment or commissioned tool at one location cannot fill the other’s missing milestone. The Camas account therefore preserves its independent geographic identity while leaving execution and accepted local output unestablished. Any later employment or public-benefit account must add evidence about the affected place rather than inherit a company-wide claim.

records.title: Yakima Basin, Washington — water storage, entitlement and delivery
records.answer: The retained August 2026 forecast describes Yakima basin water conditions and projected Yakima Project entitlements. It does not establish final delivered water, a City of Yakima outcome or a measured effect on farms, households or ecosystems.

sections.heading: Distinguish the basin from the managed delivery system
sections.text: The August 6 Reclamation release concerns the basin and Yakima Project management, including its five-reservoir context. The geographic eligibility decision counts the named basin once. A basin, a reservoir system and a project service area are related scopes, not interchangeable polygons. A service-area crosswalk is needed before a managed-project delivery total is described as covering every water user in the basin. Nothing in this place account substitutes the City of Yakima for that wider hydrologic scope.

sections.heading: Keep dates and denominators attached to the numbers
sections.text: The retained source reports August 1 storage of 605,000 acre-feet, described as 57% full and 80% of average. Those percentages refer to different comparisons and must not be averaged or read as entitlement percentages. Separately, the release projects July-to-September entitlements of 100% for senior and 58% for junior right holders. Those are class-specific forecast values, not final delivered volumes. The August 6 publication date is also distinct from the August 1 observation date.

sections.heading: Final accounting must preserve the right classes
sections.text: A later assessment should obtain the final 2026 delivered-water ledger with delivery periods, right classes, methods and entitlement denominators, and identify revisions to the August forecast. A forecast-to-final comparison needs compatible scope and units before a difference can be interpreted. Even verified water delivery would not alone measure crop effects, household welfare or ecosystem response. The present account accepts the dated forecast and storage context while admitting no final delivery series or wider outcome.

records.next_artifact: a basin/project service-area crosswalk; the final 2026 delivery accounting by right class and period, with the applicable denominators and forecast revisions. Missing final observations must not be displayed as zero delivery.
